name: Jekuthiel
overview: Jekuthiel was a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted primarily as the son of Mered and his Jewish wife. His identity is briefly recorded in Scripture, with no additional personal details or significant narrative events provided. This minimal information situates him within the genealogical context of Judah without elaboration.
namesAndTitles: The name Jekuthiel means 'G-d [El] will nourish,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in God's provision and care. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:18, was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine sustenance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jekuthiel as the son of Mered, with an explicit mention of Zanoah as his father, indicating a close familial lineage. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Jekuthiel's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of Judah, emphasizing the continuity of God's chosen people. Although his personal story is not detailed, his mention underscores the faithfulness of God's covenantal promises through successive generations. His lineage contributes to the broader biblical narrative by affirming the heritage of the tribe of Judah.
